transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Horizon - Head of Compliance), Sofia Alvarez (Horizon - IT Sec), Mark Turner (Horizon - Cloud Ops), Elena Ruiz (Horizon - Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be partial): Certification readiness check; evidence access and log retention; KMS patterns and RBAC; next steps to share reports and schedule technical deep dive.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros and then we'll jump into the artifact checklist. I'm Maya, the AE, with Liam from the SE team.

[00:12] Rajiv Menon: Hi, thanks. Quick context — Horizon is preparing for SOC2 and ISO 27001 this year, we have an external audit coming mid-June. We're looking to validate Redwood's ability to provide evidence and retention windows, and to understand the KMS flow for customer keys.

[00:31] Liam Ortiz: Great, congrats on the timeline. We'll run through what we can share — redacted SOC2 Type II report, ISO scope, our evidence portal options, RBAC/SSO patterns, and the KMS/HSM integration. Also, happy to call out how auditing access works and what logs you can export.

[00:50] Sofia Alvarez: Two immediate asks — 1) can auditors access evidence directly, read-only, without exposing customer data; 2) what are your default log retention settings and can we extend them for compliance?

[01:06] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes to both but with details. We provide a read-only evidence view in the console for authorized auditor roles and also can provide downloadable artifacts if needed. On retention, default is 90 days for high-res token traces, longer for aggregated metrics; we support export to customer S3 for long-term retention.

[01:36] Mark Turner: When you say "evidence view" — is that the Trust portal or do auditors need a Redwood account? procurement will not provision broad accounts.

[01:47] Liam Ortiz: Right, it's a couple of options — delegated access via SSO with scoped RBAC, or we can push artifacts to a pre-provisioned S3 bucket in your account. For auditors we normally recommend ephemeral access via SAML with a read-only role, so no full console access.

[02:10] Elena Ruiz: Procurement note — if auditors need a Redwood account we need a contract clause. Ephemeral SAML access would be preferred.

[02:20] Rajiv Menon: Can you walk through KMS? we run a hybrid key strategy and need to know if Redwood can integrate with our KMS/HSM or if we have to use Redwood-managed keys.

[02:33] Liam Ortiz: Sure. We support both. For hosted customers you can use Redwood-managed keys by default; for Dedicated/Private deployments we support customer-managed keys via KM S APIs — sorry transcription says KM S — and we can plug into AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own-HSM via Cloud HSM or on-prem HSM connectors.

[02:57] Sofia Alvarez: Any chance you have a diagram? in the last call it was a bit fuzzy — where are plaintext keys ever touching Redwood infra?

[03:08] Liam Ortiz: Good call. We never persist plaintext for customer-managed keys. The flow: customer KMS issues short-lived envelopes for model decryption; Redwood runtime holds only ephemeral plaintext in-GPU memory during inference and we flush caches on session end. We'll send a hardened diagram — think of it like envelope encryption with ephemeral unwrap only inside the worker.

[03:35] Mark Turner: That ephemeral memory bit — is that validated in your SOC or in your ISO scope?

[03:43] Maya Chen: The SOC2 controls around encryption and key management are covered in our Type II report; the ISO scope includes key handling policies. We'll flag the relevant sections when we share the redacted docs.

[03:58] Rajiv Menon: Ok — on logs: we need full audit chain for all admin actions, key operations, and data egress. Are those logs retained? what format — syslog, cloud audit, or something else?

[04:13] Liam Ortiz: We emit structured audit logs — for hosted that's captured in our logging pipeline and we can push to your cloud provider via subscription; formats are JSON-based events compatible with common SIEMs. Retention default 90 days but you can configure exports to S3 for long-term retention. There's also an option to increase retention on Redwood Dedicated with contract terms.

[04:35] Sofia Alvarez: Does exported S3 evidence include full stack traces or redaction applied? we can't send raw PII to auditors.

[04:44] Liam Ortiz: Exports are configurable. We can redact request payloads and only include metadata, timestamps, and decision logs. For formal audits we typically provide redacted artifacts plus a signed attestation about the redaction process.

[04:59] Elena Ruiz: procurement question: what guarantees on retention? legal needs an SLA or custody clause.

[05:06] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we can add retention and custody clauses in the contract; for hosted we offer documented processes and can provide evidence transfers into your account for long term custody. We'll follow up with suggested contract language.

[05:20] Rajiv Menon: We also need to map our internal controls to Redwood controls for ISO. Can you provide a controls matrix?

[05:28] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a controls mapping template (Redwood controls -> SOC/ISO) we usually share with customers. We'll attach it to the follow-up email.

[05:36] Mark Turner: A technical question — session KV cache and prefixes. If an auditor requests request-level payloads, are they in logs or ephemeral cache only?

[05:48] Liam Ortiz: KV cache is ephemeral and lives in GPU memory; it's not logged by default. If you need request-level logging we can enable request audit which will put event metadata into logs; payloads are subject to redaction settings. There might be additional cost.

[06:08] Rajiv Menon: Good to know. Another thread: data residency — we are regulated in EU and LatAm; some PII must stay in region. How do you guarantee region pinning?

[06:18] Liam Ortiz: We support region pinning at the deployment level — hosted customers can opt into region-specific endpoints; Dedicated and Private obviously allow you to keep data in your VPC/region. We'll need your list of regions and we'll propose an architecture with routing policy and proof of residency (artifact) for the auditors.

[06:40] Sofia Alvarez: Do you provide signed certificates or manifest proving data location for auditors?

[06:46] Maya Chen: We can produce a location attestation and include it in our ISO evidence bundle. For some enterprise agreements we add a specific SOC-type assert that workloads were pinned to region X during timeframe Y.

[07:00] Rajiv Menon: Procurement will want references or case studies of similar banks or payments companies that did the Dedicated flow.

[07:08] Elena Ruiz: yes, references important. If Redwood has a payments customer that did the on-prem or dedicated flow and completed SOC2, that would speed approval.

[07:18] Maya Chen: We can share anonymized references and case studies; we'll redact customer names but provide enough detail on architecture and controls.

[07:27] Liam Ortiz: Quick micro-demo/description — when an auditor needs evidence we can: 1) create ephemeral auditor role via SAML with scoped permissions; 2) provide read-only evidence links in the console; 3) export artifacts to your S3; all three are options.

[07:46] Rajiv Menon: If we do the S3 export path, who signs off on the artifacts? we need chain of custody.

[07:54] Liam Ortiz: The exported artifacts can be accompanied by a signed manifest and hash to verify integrity. We also time-stamp exports and include the job metadata for chain of custody.

[08:08] Mark Turner: On KMS again — do you support BYOK where the private key never leaves our HSM?

[08:17] Liam Ortiz: For obviously high-security customers we support a model where keys are stored in your HSM and Redwood only receives wrapped keys or encryption envelopes. Plaintext key material never leaves your HSM. There are additional integration steps for performance tuning.

[08:32] Sofia Alvarez: Does that add latency to inference? we need 99th percentile SLAs for latency-sensitive flows.

[08:38] Liam Ortiz: Slight overhead on initial unwrap, but we cache decrypted model shards or session keys in a secure ephemeral cache to avoid per-request unwraps. We can provide benchmark numbers — and for high-SLA use cases many customers choose Dedicated capacity where we can tune for minimal unwrap operations.

[08:58] Rajiv Menon: Can you send us the benchmarks that show encryption-related latency impact?

[09:03] Maya Chen: We'll include a small benchmark pack in the follow-up (p95 numbers with default and BYOK flows).

[09:12] Elena Ruiz: On the commercial side — if we need Dedicated for audit reasons, what is the earliest onboarding timeline?

[09:19] Maya Chen: Typical Dedicated onboard is 8-12 weeks from SOW execution; Private or on-prem tends to be longer. We'll outline options and an accelerated path if you commit to a 12-month reserved contract.

[09:34] Rajiv Menon: Good. Now, a bit of nitpicking: are API keys logged in any raw form? our policy forbids plaintext API keys in logs.

[09:44] Liam Ortiz: We never log full API keys. We emit hashed or partial-redacted identifiers for correlation, consistent with our SOC controls. We'll point to the section in the report.

[09:57] Sofia Alvarez: How about SSO — we use Okta. Do you support Just-in-Time provisioning and SCIM?

[10:05] Liam Ortiz: Yes, SAML + SCIM provisioning with role mapping is supported. JIT provisioning works for ephemeral auditor sessions as well.

[10:15] Rajiv Menon: Can you show a sample RBAC matrix? our internal control relies on separation of duties, need to confirm Redwood roles map appropriately.

[10:24] Maya Chen: We'll attach the RBAC matrix; it lists built-in roles and recommended least-privilege roles for auditors, ops, and developers.

[10:33] Mark Turner: A small technical ask: can we ingest raw audit events into our SIEM in near real-time?

[10:40] Liam Ortiz: Yes — we support streaming logs via Kafka or pushing to cloud logging endpoints; there's also a webhook option for lower-volume callbacks. Near real-time ingestion is supported for enterprise plans.

[10:54] Rajiv Menon: Sounds good. For ISO specifically, we need evidence mapping by control code. Can you map Redwood control IDs to ISO 27001 clauses?

[11:03] Maya Chen: We have a mapping spreadsheet for SOC controls to ISO clauses; we'll populate the sections relevant to your scope and share.

[11:12] Elena Ruiz: Procurement will review the contract language on audit access, encryption, and liability — can you provide standard contract clauses?

[11:21] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include suggested contract snippets and the redacted attestation.

[11:28] Sofia Alvarez: Quick question on evidence retention — if auditors request logs older than 12 months do you support retrieval?

[11:35] Liam Ortiz: If you have long-term exports to your S3, yes. If not, default hosted logs are only 90 days. For Dedicated we can contractually extend retention.

[11:47] Rajiv Menon: Let's align on immediate deliverables. Rajiv: we'd like redacted SOC2 + ISO scope; Mark: will send S3 details and retention policy; Liam: KMS runbook; Maya: RBAC matrix and contract snippets.

[11:58] Maya Chen: I'll capture that in the follow-up email. Anything else?

[12:05] Mark Turner: One more small thing — do you provide immutable audit buckets (WORM) for evidence storage?

[12:11] Liam Ortiz: We recommend customer-side WORM S3 for immutable retention. Redwood can write to that bucket on export jobs, and we can attest to the write job hashes.

[12:21] Rajiv Menon: Great. if there are no other questions, let's recap next steps.

[12:28] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll share redacted reports and mapping docs by 4/9, Liam will produce KMS runbook and benchmarks by 4/14, Mark will share retention/S3 details by 4/13, and we'll schedule a follow-up tech deep-dive in ~2 weeks.

[12:44] Elena Ruiz: Procurement will also expect anonymized references — please include in email.

[12:51] Maya Chen: Yep, we'll include those. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript. Notes: transcription has occasional mis-hears (KM S => KMS, KV cache as K-V cake in some segments), speaker turns may be slightly off.
